criteria.name: Misconduct analysis across the three charges
criteria.description: Correctly identifies and applies the governing standards for neglect/diligence, candor to the tribunal, and supervisory responsibility, distinguishing conceded from contested elements.

subcriteria.name: Neglect and diligence
subcriteria.description: Analyzes the missed service deadline and post-departure monitoring as a diligence failure; correctly frames concession and its limits.

subcriteria.name: Candor to the tribunal
subcriteria.description: Analyzes the affidavit date under the false-statement standard; distinguishes a knowing misstatement from an honest reconstruction and grapples honestly with the interview facts.

subcriteria.name: Supervisory responsibility
subcriteria.description: Analyzes the reliance on a single staff member's personal calendar as a supervision/systems failure and the effect of remedial measures.

criteria.name: Sanction analysis and proportionality
criteria.description: Builds a proportional-sanction argument from aggravating and mitigating factors and comparable outcomes, keyed to the purposes of discipline.

subcriteria.name: Aggravating and mitigating factors
subcriteria.description: Marshals the recognized factors accurately, including the September notice and false client reassurance as aggravation and the clean record, cooperation, remedial steps, and personal circumstances as mitigation.

subcriteria.name: Comparable-outcome reasoning
subcriteria.description: Uses comparable disciplinary outcomes to argue for a proportional sanction rather than relying on sympathy.

criteria.name: Respondent's pre-hearing brief
criteria.description: A well-structured, rule-compliant, persuasive brief appropriate to the disciplinary posture and standard of review.

subcriteria.name: Structure and rule compliance
subcriteria.description: Organization, format, and procedural compliance for the referee/Supreme Court posture.

subcriteria.name: Argument and standard of review
subcriteria.description: Persuasive argument that correctly deploys the applicable standard of review and burden.

criteria.name: Fact development and client counseling
criteria.description: Reconstructs a defensible timeline from record and interviews and counsels a distressed client, including on the candor problem.

subcriteria.name: Timeline reconstruction
subcriteria.description: Accurately distinguishes when the client knew from when she says she knew, tested against the record.

subcriteria.name: Counseling the distressed client
subcriteria.description: Interviews with rapport, surfaces gated facts appropriately, and counsels ethically on the misstatement; recognizes the Rule 4.2 boundary with the former client.

criteria.name: Oral argument readiness
criteria.description: Prepared, responsive oral argument before the referee, fielding questions on the candor charge and sanction.
